system:
You write the executive summary of a technical evaluation for a recruiter
(medium technical knowledge). 3-5 sentences, clear English, no gratuitous jargon.
Say: overall quality, the most important finding (if any) in terms she will understand,
and what to verify in the interview. If role_requirements are present, say in one
sentence how well the candidate appears to meet what the role asks. Factual tone —
neither salesy nor alarmist.
Respond with JSON ONLY: {"summary": "..."}
user: {"notebook": "nb01_ana_ferreira.ipynb", "decision": "AVANCAR", "scores": {"C1": 5, "C2": 5, "C3": 5, "C4": 5}, "justifications": {"C1": "Cell 7 performs a stratified train/test split before any fitting, and uses a Pipeline+ColumnTransformer so scaling/encoding are learned on X_tr only (no leakage). The notebook also explicitly handles the stated data messiness (comma decimals, mixed date formats, inconsistent categories, missing values) in cell 3 and reports zero remaining nulls.", "C2": "All code cells execute end-to-end with no exceptions (cells 1, 3, 5, 7–9 show successful outputs). Randomness is controlled via random_state in train_test_split and LogisticRegression (cell 7), supporting stable results.", "C3": "The conclusion cites AUC 0.729, which matches the executed metric AUC_TEST=0.729 in cell 8 (within ±0.01). Other described drivers are consistent with the printed top coefficients in cell 9 (e.g., contract type, complaints, late payment).", "C4": "Conclusions are directly supported by the model outputs: AUC is reported (cell 8) and drivers are tied to coefficients (cell 9), leading to a concrete retention recommendation for monthly-contract customers with complaints. The narrative also appropriately acknowledges the low recall at the default threshold (cell 8) and proposes threshold calibration and temporal validation as next steps (cell 10)."}, "findings": [], "role_requirements": "not provided"}

response.summary: Overall, the notebook is high quality: it runs end-to-end, is reproducible, and uses a proper train/test split with a preprocessing pipeline that avoids data leakage. The key finding is a solid-but-not-perfect model performance (AUC ~0.73) and a clear business signal that customers on monthly contracts—especially those with complaints and late payments—are more likely to churn, though recall at the default threshold is low. In the interview, verify she can clearly explain how the Pipeline/ColumnTransformer prevents leakage, what AUC means in business terms, and how she would choose a decision threshold (and evaluate it) to improve recall without creating too many false alarms. Also ask how she would set up a time-based/temporal validation to ensure the model holds up in production.
